items.headline: BOJ hikes to 1.25%, highest since 1995, board splits 7-2 as yen fails to rally
items.summary: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.25% on Sept 18, the sixth hike since exiting ultra-loose policy and the fastest pace of tightening since 1990, with board members Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato dissenting in a 7-2 vote. Despite the hike, the yen failed to strengthen meaningfully even as JGB yields climbed, with Governor Ueda signaling further moves are likely given inflation risk skewed to the upside.
items.actionable: The yen's failure to rally on a hawkish BOJ hike suggests carry-trade unwind risk to HK tech and Asia risk assets is less acute than feared for Monday's open, but Ueda's signal of more hikes ahead keeps the tail risk alive for 0700.HK/0981.HK/1810.HK into Q4.

items.headline: Oil sinks ~6% Friday as Saudi pipeline restoration offsets widening Houthi attacks
items.summary: WTI (CL=F) closed down 6.3% to $95.47 and Brent (BZ=F) fell 5.8% to $98.77 on Sept 18 as signs that Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is coming back online eased supply-disruption fears, even as Houthi forces extended a fresh wave of strikes on Saudi energy and military sites in Abha, Najran and Jazan. The kingdom's main eastern crude fields were not targeted, limiting the near-term production impact.
items.actionable: A sharp oil-price drop eases the inflation-driven case for further Fed hikes, a tailwind for gold/silver carry costs, but the still-live Houthi threat to Saudi infrastructure (first sustained breach of the 2022-2026 truce) keeps a geopolitical safe-haven bid underneath the metals book.

items.headline: Gold and silver hit weekly highs Friday, silver spikes above $67.80 intraday
items.summary: Gold futures (GC=F) closed Sept 18 at $4,415.90 (+0.37%) after touching a weekly high of $4,439.80, while silver (SI=F) closed at $66.79 (+2.0%) after spiking to $67.90 intraday, extending Thursday's post-Fed-hike rebound. Easing oil prices and fading near-term inflation fear were cited as tailwinds even as GDX (-0.46%) and SILJ (+0.30%) diverged from the metals' gains on Friday's session.
items.actionable: Two straight up days in metals after the hawkish Fed hike reinforces the bull case underpinning the core silver/miner book, but Friday's miner underperformance versus spot (GDX -0.46%, HL -0.21% vs silver +2.0%) is worth watching for a leverage-unwind signal into Monday's open.

items.headline: S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq rally as markets shrug off Fed's hawkish hike
items.summary: US stocks recovered Thursday with the S&P 500 up 1.14% to 7,637.76, the Dow up 0.61%, and the Nasdaq up 1.69%, a day after selling off on the Fed's 25bp hike. The S&P added a further 0.17% to 7,650.50 on Friday, with futures still pricing additional hikes given 16 of 18 officials project more tightening this year.
items.actionable: A sharp risk-on rebound in the two sessions after a hawkish hike is broadly supportive for equity beta and miners riding the risk-on tape, but the market's fast forgiveness of hawkish Fed signaling raises the odds of a similarly sharp reversal if the hike-per-quarter pace continues into Q4.

items.headline: SMIC jumps 4.4% on Goldman upgrade and cloud-AI tailwind while Tencent slides to a multi-week low
items.summary: SMIC (0981.HK) closed Sept 18 up 4.4% to HK$65.15 after Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month target price to HK$73.1 (from HK$63.7) on rising demand from China's fabless/chip-design customers, part of a broader Hong Kong tech pop tracking Oracle's strong cloud-infrastructure guidance. Tencent (0700.HK) instead fell a third straight session to HK$419.00 (-1.6%), its lowest close in weeks, as the broader Hang Seng traded in a holding pattern awaiting concrete Beijing stimulus signals.
items.actionable: The book's HK tech sleeve is diverging sharply -- SMIC's AI-driven upgrade cycle is working while Tencent grinds to fresh multi-week lows -- so any near-term Beijing stimulus headline is the key catalyst that could re-rate 0700.HK, while 0981.HK momentum looks more analyst-upgrade-driven and less dependent on policy.

items.headline: Bitcoin and ether rise Friday, shrugging off the Senate's failed CLARITY Act vote
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed from $76,350 to nearly $78,000 and ether rose from $2,445 toward $2,500 in Friday Sept 18 trading, with investors moving past Tuesday's failed CLARITY Act cloture vote to look toward the next legislative push for crypto market-structure rules. The move came alongside the broader post-Fed-hike risk-on rebound across equities.
items.actionable: No direct crypto holdings in this portfolio, but crypto shrugging off a real regulatory setback to rally alongside equities and metals confirms Friday's move was a broad risk-on rebound rather than an asset-specific short squeeze -- useful read-through for gauging whether Monday's silver/miner strength can extend.

items.headline: Silver squeeze thesis intact: COMEX registered inventories down ~70% since 2020, LBMA down ~40%
items.summary: COMEX registered silver inventories have fallen roughly 70-75% from 2020 highs to about 79.9 million ounces, while LBMA holdings are down about 40%, with the World Silver Survey 2026 projecting a sixth consecutive annual deficit of 46.3 million ounces. China also implemented new export licensing restrictions on refined silver starting January 1, 2026.
items.actionable: Persistent physical tightness in deliverable silver supports the structural bull case underpinning the AG/HL/PAAS/SILJ/SLVP positions, reinforcing that this week's pullback-then-rebound was more a leverage/liquidity event than a change in fundamentals.

items.headline: Tencent buys back HK$550.9m of shares as AI capex ramps sharply
items.summary: Tencent repurchased 856,000 shares for HK$550.9 million on Sept 15, continuing its buyback program even as it doubles AI investment to over RMB 36bn in 2026 from RMB 18bn in 2025; Q2 capex rose 65% YoY to RMB 52.8bn. The stock has kept sliding since, down to HK$419 by Sept 18, roughly 29% off its highs on competition and AI-spending concerns.
items.actionable: Continued buybacks signal management confidence in 0700.HK even as the stock grinds to fresh multi-week lows -- a hold-the-line signal rather than a catalyst, and the buyback pace is modest relative to market cap so it is unlikely to arrest the slide on its own.

items.headline: DBS, OCBC and UOB complete first live blockchain-enabled SGD interbank transactions
items.summary: Singapore's three largest banks executed live domestic SGD transactions using tokenised deposits on Swift's blockchain-based ledger on Sept 10, the first time they've done so interbank, building on Swift's July 2026 rollout across 17 banks.
items.actionable: Incremental long-term positive for DBS's transaction-banking franchise and Singapore's fintech-hub positioning, though not a near-term earnings driver; D05.SI closed Friday roughly flat at S$76.86.

items.headline: Gold ETFs hit record $4,189-tonne holdings on record August inflows, while silver ETFs saw pre-FOMC outflows
items.summary: The World Gold Council's August report showed global gold-backed ETFs added $18bn, the second-largest monthly inflow on record, lifting holdings to an all-time high of 4,189 tonnes ($615bn AUM). In the five trading days into Sept 8, SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) took in $1,378m while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) saw a $29m outflow, a divergence that reversed once the Fed hike hit and silver rallied hard.
items.actionable: Record institutional gold demand into September, plus the subsequent silver rebound once positioning was shaken out, together support the broad-based conviction case for the GDX/SILJ/miners side of the book heading into next week.
